text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- Engineering and offshore group Aker ASA is no longer considering a merger with investment group RGI. The two companies apparently could not agree on the exchange value of the shares.

- NorWatch, a non-profit group, has examined the behaviour of 800 Norwegian companies active in the Third World in an effort to make them do business with more responsibility. NorWatch says the survey uncovered several cases where companies could be subjected to criticism.
- During the first half of 1996 seven of 11 Norwegian cruise and passengers ships inspected in foreign ports were found to have violated safety regulations.

- Norwegian authorities are speeding up the dismantling of the last controversial import quotas on clothes and textiles. This is bad news for Norwegian textile producers, who say it is unfortunate that Norway now is getting "more liberal than the EU".
- House construction decreases while the largest companies are likely to increase their share of the market to 25-27 percent this year from 23.8 percent in 1995.
